text:
If you’re heading out for sunset, there’s still a decent view to work with, with clouds thinning toward a partly cloudy evening and sunset at 7:26. West winds stay light, the lake should remain calm with waves a foot or less, and the temperature will ease from the low 80s toward a comfortable 63 overnight. Patchy fog may briefly show up around 3 or 4 in the morning, but it shouldn’t be a major player.

Friday looks mostly sunny and a little cooler, with a high in the upper 70s. The official forecast carries just a slight chance of a shower after noon, though the models aren’t fully aligned, so I’d keep a rain jacket handy without rearranging the day around it. Winds on the lake turn light and variable, then northwest near 10 knots, with small waves. Good evening plans tonight, and fine daytime outdoor plans tomorrow, but keep an eye on the sky after lunch.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): High pressure anchors directly over Vermont and the North Country for Sunday and Labor Day, delivering ideal holiday weekend weather. Sunday will be bright, sunny, and crisp with highs near 72°. Labor Day (Monday) brings full sunshine, light winds, and pleasant highs warming to near 76°—offering picture-perfect conditions for outdoor holiday plans. A weak cold front crosses Monday night into Tuesday, bringing scattered overnight shower chances (30% chance) and highs near 70° Tuesday, before additional passing disturbances bring periodic shower chances (50% chance) through the middle of next week with highs remaining in the 70s.
